transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I keep messing up things at work that I really should be catching. I’m a supervisor, so I’m dealing with sales reports and checking procedures, and I’ll copy the wrong number off the team dashboard or miss a line I was supposed to review—even when I honestly thought I went back over it.

It’s frustrating, because it feels like dumb mistakes, you know? Like stuff I know how to do. And then I start thinking about how the dashboard layout changed a while back, and how everyone complains about it, but still… I’m the one handing in the report with the wrong number. That’s the kind of thing that made me think I should come talk to someone.
How do you feel about yourself when you make these mistakes at work?

I mean… not great, honestly. I mostly just feel embarrassed, like I should’ve caught it. Then I start replaying the whole thing in my head—where I got the number from, whether the dashboard was showing the weekly or monthly view, stuff like that—and I kind of get stuck on it.

It’s weird because I know everyone makes mistakes, and half the team complains about the system too, but when it’s me turning it in, it feels like… come on, man, you’re supposed to be the one checking this. So yeah, I guess I feel pretty down on myself in the moment.
Are these mistakes at work affecting your relationships with your colleagues or your overall job performance?

Yeah… I mean, I guess that’s kind of why I finally came in. It’s not just me feeling bad about it anymore. My manager actually put it in a formal review, like documented that I’m making errors and not following through consistently, which felt pretty awful.

And with colleagues it’s… mostly embarrassing. Like, I don’t think everyone hates me or anything, but I can tell it affects how much people want to rely on me.

At home too, honestly. It turns into arguments because I’ll say I’m going to take care of something and then it doesn’t happen, or it’s half-done, and then people feel like they can’t count on me. Which… yeah, I get why they’d feel that way, but it still sucks to hear.
Have you noticed any impact on your daily life or overall well-being beyond just the work and home issues you've mentioned?

Yeah, I mean… it kind of bleeds into everything, I guess. Like it’s not just “oh, I made a mistake on a report.” At work it’s gotten serious enough that my manager put it in a formal review, which is… you know, that follows you around.

And then outside of work, it turns into this whole thing where people feel like they can’t count on me to actually follow through. Like I’ll say I’m going to handle something, and then somehow it becomes a whole argument later. It’s stressful. And then I start thinking about whether I’m just being careless, or if I’m overpromising, or—honestly, sometimes I get stuck thinking about the review itself and what it means for my job.

So yeah, it’s affecting my day-to-day. It’s hard not to carry that around.
Do you feel like these mistakes and the stress they cause are interfering with your ability to enjoy things you normally like to do?

I don’t know… maybe a little? I haven’t really kept track of it like that.

Like, I’ll still try to watch a game or go do something I usually like, but sometimes my head is still kind of back at work, thinking about the mistake or what my manager thinks. But then other times I’m fine once I’m actually doing the thing.

Sorry, I’m kind of rambling. I guess I’m not sure if I’d say it’s stopping me from enjoying stuff, exactly. It’s more like the stress follows me around sometimes.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

I’m not sure. I mean, I worry when there’s something to worry about, like the work stuff or if I know I messed something up. But “no obvious reason”… I don’t know if I’d describe it that way.

Sometimes I’ll be sitting there and my brain kind of grabs onto something, but usually there’s some thread to it, even if it’s dumb. Like I’ll remember I was supposed to call someone back, and then that makes me think of three other things, and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I paid the insurance thing—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

I guess I haven’t really noticed myself worrying out of nowhere. It’s more tied to whatever’s going on.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless?

Yeah, definitely. Especially if I’m stuck sitting for a while, like in a long meeting. It’s like my body is buzzing inside or something, and I’m trying to look normal, but I’m shifting in my chair, tapping my foot, messing with a pen.

Sometimes I’ll make up a reason to step out, like get water or check on something, just because sitting there feels… I don’t know, almost impossible after a while. And then I’ll come back and try to settle down again, but it builds back up.
Do you often find yourself having trouble focusing on what's being said in conversations?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, if someone’s talking directly to me I’m usually trying to listen, but it’s easy for something else to pull me off before I realize it.

Like at work, if I’m reviewing call notes or looking at numbers and there’s a conversation going on across the room, I’ll suddenly be listening to that instead. Or I’ll get some random thought about something at home, like, did I leave something out or do I need to handle something later, and then I’ve lost the thread.

Sorry, you asked about conversations specifically—yeah, it happens there too, where I’ll have to kind of catch back up and pretend I didn’t miss part of what they said.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain tasks or situations because they make you feel anxious or overwhelmed?

I’m not sure I’d say anxious, exactly. Overwhelmed maybe sometimes, but… I don’t know, it depends what you mean.

Like if there’s a big pile of stuff to do, I might put it off because I don’t know where to start, and then I end up doing some smaller thing instead. But that’s not always because I’m scared of it. It’s more like my brain just kind of refuses to line it up.

At work, there are certain reports or longer emails I’ll avoid starting, and then I’ll go check on something else, or talk to someone about a different issue, and then suddenly it’s an hour later. Actually, that reminds me, I did that yesterday with—sorry. Yeah, I guess I do avoid some tasks when they feel like too much, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxiety.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're not good enough?

I don’t know… not really “worthless,” I don’t think. Like, I get frustrated with myself when I mess something up or don’t get something done the way I meant to, but that feels different than thinking I’m not good enough as a person.

I mean, at work sometimes if I’m behind on something, I’ll start comparing myself to other supervisors who seem like they’ve got everything organized, and then I’ll think, “Why can’t I just do it like that?” But then I’ll get distracted by some other fire to put out—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So… no, I don’t think I often feel worthless. More like annoyed with myself sometimes.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened?

Guilty… not usually, I don’t think. I mean, if I forget to follow up on something or I say I’ll do something and then it slips, I feel bad about it, sure. Especially if someone else has to remind me.

But guilty about things that have happened, like in a bigger way? I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say that’s something I’m sitting around thinking about all the time. Sometimes I’ll replay a conversation and think, “I should’ve handled that better,” but then I’m usually onto the next thing I need to deal with. So… maybe a little sometimes, but not often.
Do you often criticize yourself for your mistakes?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I do sometimes. If I make a mistake, I’ll be annoyed with myself, like, “Come on, why didn’t you catch that?” Especially if it’s something simple.

But I don’t know if I’d say I’m constantly criticizing myself. It’s more like in the moment I’ll beat myself up a little, and then something else comes up and I’m dealing with that. Like at work, if I miss something in a report—well, reports are kind of a whole thing anyway—but then I’ll think about how I should’ve slowed down and checked it better.

So… sometimes, yes. Not all the time, I don’t think.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge, even when there's no apparent reason to feel that way?

Nervous or on edge… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say for no reason, exactly. Like if there’s something going on at work, or I know I’ve got a bunch of stuff I haven’t gotten to yet, then yeah, I can feel kind of keyed up.

But if everything’s fine? I don’t know that I’m just sitting there feeling nervous out of nowhere. Sometimes I’m restless, or I feel like I should be doing something, but that’s not really the same as nervous, I don’t think.

Sorry, I’m trying to think of an example, but nothing specific is coming to mind. So… maybe sometimes, but I wouldn’t say often for no reason.
Do you find that your mind often wanders even when you're trying to focus on something?

Yeah, that happens a lot. Like, I’ll be trying to review call notes or go over numbers, and then I’ll hear one conversation across the room and I’m suddenly listening to that instead, before I even realize I’ve stopped working.

Or sometimes it’s not even something in the room—it’ll be some random thought about something at home, like whether I remembered to do some little thing, and then I’m off on that for a minute. Then I look back at the notes and I’m like, “Wait, where was I?” So yeah, my mind wanders pretty often when I’m supposed to be focusing.
Do you find it difficult to complete tasks because you lose interest or get distracted, rather than because you're worried about doing them perfectly?

Yeah, more that than worrying about it being perfect. Like if my manager gives me three or four things to handle, I’ll start off fine—like, okay, I’ve got this, I’ll knock these out—and then somebody asks me a question, or I get pulled into something else, or I see an issue with one of the reps and go deal with that.

And then later, sometimes way later, I’ll realize I never sent the follow-up email or I didn’t close out the coaching note. Which is annoying because it’s not like I was sitting there stressing over whether the wording was perfect. I just kind of… got off track. Then I’m trying to remember where I left it, and by then there’s already another thing happening.
Do you have difficulty waiting for your turn in lines or when waiting for something to happen?

Yeah, I do. Lines are bad for me—not like I’m yelling at people or anything, but I get impatient fast. Same thing if I’m on hold with a vendor, I’m already thinking, “Come on, let’s go,” and I’ll start looking for some other way to get it handled.

Even in meetings, if another supervisor is talking and it’s taking a while to get to the point, I’ll feel myself wanting to jump in or move it along. I know people need their turn, but sitting there waiting for it to happen is… yeah, it gets under my skin pretty quickly.
Do you have trouble organizing your work or daily activities?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I have systems, kind of, like notes and lists, but whether I’m “organized” is probably not what my wife would say. Work can get messy depending on the day.

Like, I’ll write something down on a sticky note, then I’ve got another note in my phone, and then someone will hand me a paper with numbers on it, and now it’s three different places. Actually, that reminds me, I used to have this one notebook I was trying to use for everything, but then I left it in my truck for like a week and started using scraps of paper again.

So… yeah, I guess I have some trouble with it, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by organizing.
Do you find that these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and completing tasks are happening most days?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s been a real problem since I moved into the supervisor role, which was about… a year and two months ago, I think.

Before that I mean, I had stuff here and there, but this is when it really started showing up because now there’s always something coming at me. Like, I’ll be in the middle of one thing and then—sorry, I know I’m kind of wandering—but yeah, since taking that role, it’s been pretty consistent most days.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and restlessness for most of your life?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, it’s hard to remember everything from when I was a kid, but my mom definitely says I was like this back then too.

She’ll bring up these notes teachers sent home in elementary school—stuff like I rushed through my work, lost homework, talked out of turn. And I guess I had a hard time staying in my seat unless somebody reminded me. Which is funny because my mom kept a bunch of those papers in this old folder, and every once in a while she’ll pull something out like, “See, this isn’t new.”

So… yeah, it does seem like it’s been most of my life, not just recently.
Do you find that you have trouble focusing or get restless in most situations, not just at work?

Yeah, it’s not just work. Work is where it’s gotten the most obvious, I guess, because my manager actually put it in a formal review, which was pretty embarrassing.

But at home too… it causes problems. Like people feel like they can’t really count on me to follow through on stuff. And then I’ll try to explain, but it sounds like excuses, and then we end up arguing about that instead of the original thing. So, yeah, it shows up in more than one place.

doctor.question: Do you find it difficult to complete tasks because you lose interest or get distracted, rather than because you're worried about doing them perfectly?

target_item.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: If my manager gives me three or four things to handle, I usually start strong, but then I get pulled into something else and later realize I never sent the follow-up email or closed out the coaching note.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly about difficulty completing tasks due to losing interest or getting distracted, rather than perfectionistic worry.

patient.answer:
Yeah, more that than worrying about it being perfect. Like if my manager gives me three or four things to handle, I’ll start off fine—like, okay, I’ve got this, I’ll knock these out—and then somebody asks me a question, or I get pulled into something else, or I see an issue with one of the reps and go deal with that.

And then later, sometimes way later, I’ll realize I never sent the follow-up email or I didn’t close out the coaching note. Which is annoying because it’s not like I was sitting there stressing over whether the wording was perfect. I just kind of… got off track. Then I’m trying to remember where I left it, and by then there’s already another thing happening.

inference.note: F43.8 was ruled out due to lack of clear evidence of adjustment disorder, and the patient's symptoms seem to align more closely with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (F90.0) or other anxiety disorders (F41.8)

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's symptoms are better explained by attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or another condition such as anxiety disorder
doctor.question: Do you have difficulty waiting for your turn in lines or when waiting for something to happen?

target_item.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: Waiting my turn, whether it's in a line, on hold with a vendor, or while another supervisor is talking, makes me impatient fast and I start pushing to move things along.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about difficulty waiting for a turn in lines or while waiting for something to happen, which directly matches this symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I do. Lines are bad for me—not like I’m yelling at people or anything, but I get impatient fast. Same thing if I’m on hold with a vendor, I’m already thinking, “Come on, let’s go,” and I’ll start looking for some other way to get it handled.

Even in meetings, if another supervisor is talking and it’s taking a while to get to the point, I’ll feel myself wanting to jump in or move it along. I know people need their turn, but sitting there waiting for it to happen is… yeah, it gets under my skin pretty quickly.

inference.note: Added F90.8 as the patient's symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and restlessness are consistent with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and also considered F90.0 as the symptoms of impulsivity and difficulty waiting in lines are more pronounced

doctor.intent: determine if the patient has difficulty organizing tasks and activities
doctor.question: Do you have trouble organizing your work or daily activities?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about difficulty organizing tasks or activities, but the provided symptom profile does not include an organizing-difficulty item. Related items like follow-through problems are not the same as organization difficulties.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I have systems, kind of, like notes and lists, but whether I’m “organized” is probably not what my wife would say. Work can get messy depending on the day.

Like, I’ll write something down on a sticky note, then I’ve got another note in my phone, and then someone will hand me a paper with numbers on it, and now it’s three different places. Actually, that reminds me, I used to have this one notebook I was trying to use for everything, but then I left it in my truck for like a week and started using scraps of paper again.

So… yeah, I guess I have some trouble with it, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by organizing.

inference.note: Added F90.9 as the patient's symptoms of inattention, disorganization, and impulsivity are consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Unspecified, and ruled out F41.8 as the patient does not exhibit significant anxiety symptoms

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are persistent and interfere with daily life
doctor.question: Do you find that these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and completing tasks are happening most days?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been a real problem since I moved into the supervisor role about 1 year and 2 months ago.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about how persistent/frequent the symptoms are over time, which is best matched by the duration item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s been a real problem since I moved into the supervisor role, which was about… a year and two months ago, I think.

Before that I mean, I had stuff here and there, but this is when it really started showing up because now there’s always something coming at me. Like, I’ll be in the middle of one thing and then—sorry, I know I’m kind of wandering—but yeah, since taking that role, it’s been pretty consistent most days.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are persistent and long-standing
doctor.question: Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and restlessness for most of your life?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: I was like this as a kid too—my mom still talks about teacher notes from elementary school saying I rushed through work, lost homework, talked out of turn, and couldn't stay seated without being reminded.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the focus and restlessness difficulties have been present for most of life, which directly relates to childhood onset before age 12.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I think so. I mean, it’s hard to remember everything from when I was a kid, but my mom definitely says I was like this back then too.

She’ll bring up these notes teachers sent home in elementary school—stuff like I rushed through my work, lost homework, talked out of turn. And I guess I had a hard time staying in my seat unless somebody reminded me. Which is funny because my mom kept a bunch of those papers in this old folder, and every once in a while she’ll pull something out like, “See, this isn’t new.”

So… yeah, it does seem like it’s been most of my life, not just recently.

doctor.intent: determine if symptoms are persistent across different situations
doctor.question: Do you find that you have trouble focusing or get restless in most situations, not just at work?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work it has gotten to the point that my manager put it in a formal review, and at home it adds to conflict because people feel like they can't count on me to follow through.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the ADHD-related difficulties occur across multiple settings, not just work; this profile best covers impairment in both work and home contexts.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it’s not just work. Work is where it’s gotten the most obvious, I guess, because my manager actually put it in a formal review, which was pretty embarrassing.

But at home too… it causes problems. Like people feel like they can’t really count on me to follow through on stuff. And then I’ll try to explain, but it sounds like excuses, and then we end up arguing about that instead of the original thing. So, yeah, it shows up in more than one place.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, as well as the duration and pervasive nature of these symptoms across multiple settings, are consistent with a diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Type (F90.0).
